desc: Iterate through each index `i` in `nums` treating `nums[i]` as the candidate for the unique middle mode.
For each candidate, count the occurrences of `nums[i]` in the left subarray (`nums[:i]`) and right subarray (`nums[i+1:]`).

Calculate the number of ways to form valid subsequences by selecting 2 elements from the left and 2 from the right such that the total count of the middle element is strictly greater than the count of any other selected element.
If the middle element appears exactly twice in the subsequence (once left, once right), ensure no other element appears twice.
If the middle element appears three times, ensure no other element appears twice or more.
If the middle element appears four times, any other elements are fine as long as they don't reach 4 (which is impossible with only 2 slots per side).
Sum the counts for all valid candidates modulo $10^9 + 7$.

Implement the solution class with helper functions for combinations and the elementary symmetric polynomial $e_3$, then execute the main logic iterating through each element as the potential middle mode.
Run the code against the provided examples to verify correctness.
Check edge cases (e.g., all elements same, all elements distinct).
Ensure the modulo operation is applied correctly at each addition/multiplication step.
